Digital Literacy is a core competency, not one of the 15 learning area headings for Grade 4–6.
In senior school, Community Service Learning appears as a subject in the Humanities & Business Studies track course lists.

children.topic: A track = a group of subjects
children.note: Each pathway has tracks, which are combinations of related subjects.

children.topic: A track is a group of subjects
children.note: Inside each pathway are tracks. A track is a combination of related subjects, for example Pure Sciences inside STEM.

children.topic: Able to use what you learn

Learners grow crops, care for soil and learn about animals. At home: start a small kitchen garden or sack garden with sukuma wiki or spinach.
Science used in daily life: growing food, computers and running a healthy home. Subjects: Agriculture, Computer Studies, Home Science, Information Communication
Learners start with greetings, letters and simple sentences. At home: practise a few greetings together each day.
Activity-based areas grow into subjects such as Science and Technology, Social Studies and Agriculture.
Creating and performing: songs, dance, plays, films and visual art. Subjects: Music and Dance, Theatre and Film, Fine Arts.
Tracks: Arts (music and dance, theatre and film, fine arts) and Sports Science. Suits learners with creative or sporting talent.

children.topic: Ask: which schools offer this track?
children.note: Not every school offers every track or subject. Check what nearby schools offer before deciding.
Citizenship is one of the seven core competencies: being a responsible, caring member of society.
Teachers check learning day by day through observation, questions, oral reading and short tasks.
Children arrive from two years of pre-primary, where they learnt through play. Grade 1 builds gently on that.
Learners join junior school after finishing Grade 6 in upper primary.
After PP2, children join Grade 1. KICD's 2019 framework says Grade 1 starts at about age 6.
Speaking, listening, writing and working well with others. Example: siblings planning together how to share the chores.
Speaking, listening, writing and working well with others — for example presenting a group project.
Learners use what they learn to help meet a real need in their community, then reflect on it in class.
Christian Religious Education: Bible stories, prayer, and values like love, kindness and sharing.
Christian Religious Education: Bible stories and how to live them out daily. At home: talk about a story and one way to show kindness this week.
Drawing, colouring, modelling, music, singing, dance and movement games that grow imagination and healthy bodies.
Art, music, movement and play that build imagination and strong bodies.
Learners draw, paint, make crafts, sing, play music and perform. At home: make a toy or musical shaker from bottle tops and a used bottle.
Thinking things through and finding solutions. Example: working out why the tomato seedlings are wilting and what to change.
Using phones, computers and the internet safely and well. Example: looking up the weather with a parent and talking about safe use.
Using the toilet, eating, dressing and packing a bag without much help.
Official papers group levels: Early Years = pre-primary plus lower primary; Middle School = upper primary plus junior school.
Empowerment = helping parents gain the know-how to support children. Engagement = parents taking an active part with teachers.
KICD's 2019 timeline shows a national assessment at the end of Grade 3. Check the current name and timing with your school or KNEC.
There is a national assessment at the end of Grade 6 — check the current name and timing with your school or KNEC.
Reading longer texts, writing essays and letters, speaking in debates, and using grammar correctly.
Learners read stories, write short compositions and speak in class. At home: let your child read a label, a newspaper headline or a short story aloud to you.
Children listen, speak, read and write in English: sounds, words, short stories, and simple sentences about daily life.
Exploring home, school and nature: weather, plants, animals, water, keeping clean and staying safe.
Learning about the world around them: themselves, family, home, plants, animals, weather, and keeping clean and safe.
Teachers watch, ask questions and check work during lessons to see what each child can do and what help they need next.
Teachers watch, ask questions, check written work and give feedback. This is called formative assessment.

children.note: KICD lists designs for these four. Schools offer them only where they have teachers, so ask which ones your school has.
Lower primary is three years: Grade 1, Grade 2 and Grade 3.
Senior school lasts three years: Grade 10, Grade 11 and Grade 12.
Upper primary is three school years: Grade 4, Grade 5 and Grade 6.
Junior school covers three grades: Grade 7, Grade 8 and Grade 9.
The 2019 framework called it Pre-Technical and Pre-Career Education, linking technical skills with career awareness.
Earlier designs had a separate hygiene and nutrition area; today such topics appear within other areas.
Telling the truth and keeping promises. Example: returning extra change to the shopkeeper.
How people live, believe, govern, trade and look after places. Subjects: Christian Religious Education (CRE), Islamic Religious Education (IRE), Community Servi
Learning in the language of the local community, through stories, songs and talk, to value home language and culture.
Learners study science as one subject that mixes the living world, materials and energy. They do experiments, observe carefully and record results.
Islamic Religious Education: stories, short surahs, prayer and good manners taught in Islam.
Junior school is the second half of middle school, for three years.
Three years of junior school (junior secondary), with areas such as Integrated Science and Pre-Technical Studies.
The Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development (set up by Act No. 4 of 2013) develops CBC designs and approves course books.
KICD's 2024 list shows Kiswahili materials for PP2. Children hear and use simple Kiswahili words, greetings, songs and stories.
Listening, speaking, early reading and early writing, mostly through stories, songs and talk.
Reading, writing, speaking and enjoying stories in Kenyan and foreign languages. Subjects: English, Literature in English, Kiswahili, Fasihi ya Kiswahili, Arabi
Unlike earlier levels, each learner follows one pathway that matches their interests, strengths and hoped-for careers.
Young children learn best by doing: playing, singing, building, drawing and talking. Pre-primary is built around this, not around long written work.
Community Service Learning also appears as a senior school subject in the Social Sciences pathway lists.
Children build reading, writing and number skills. Grade 1 starts at about age 6.
Early number work through counting, sorting and playing with real objects.
Counting, numbers, adding and taking away, shapes, measuring and money. Course books call it Mathematical Activities.
Learners work with whole numbers, fractions, money, measurement and shapes. At home: at the market, ask how much change you should get, or measure flour for cha
Recognising Kenyan coins and notes, and pretend buying and selling.

children.topic: National assessment at end of Grade 9
children.note: There is a national assessment at the end of Grade 9. Check the current name and timing with your school or KNEC.
National assessments come at the end of Grade 3, Grade 6 and Grade 9. Check the current names and timing with your school or KNEC.

children.topic: National examination at end of Grade 12
children.note: There is expected to be a national assessment at the end of Grade 12. Check the current name, format and timing with KNEC or your school.
KICD's Grade 7 page lists Integrated Science and Pre-Technical Studies, which are new after Grade 6.
CBC has 2 years pre-primary, 6 primary, 3 junior school and 3 senior school before college or university.
Upper primary is Grade 4 to Grade 6, part of Middle School.
Pre-primary plus lower primary (Grades 1–3) together make the early years stage (Early Years Education).
The 2019 curriculum framework groups upper primary and junior school together as middle school.
KICD's 2019 framework groups upper primary (Grade 4–6) and junior school (Grade 7–9) together as middle school.
Pre-primary and lower primary together make up Early Years Education in the CBC structure.
Mix flour, salt, water and a little oil. Rolling and squeezing strengthens fingers for writing.
A portfolio is a collection of a child's work over time. KICD's parent guidelines mention portfolios and learners' diaries as records.
Two years of nursery before Grade 1. Learning is mostly through play, songs and stories.
A practical learning area that introduces technical work: using tools and materials safely, making things and understanding the world of work. Check the current
Science and maths studied in depth, the base for medicine, engineering and research. Subjects: Core Mathematics, Essential Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry, Phys
Even 15 minutes of reading anything — stories, newspapers, labels — grows vocabulary.

children.topic: Read or tell a story daily
children.note: Ten minutes a day is enough. Old stories from grandparents count too.
The 2024 list names Christian Religious Education and Islamic Religious Education for pre-primary. Families usually follow the option that matches their faith;
Learners study one: Christian, Islamic or Hindu Religious Education. It covers faith, moral values and how to live well with others.
Doing your chores, caring for your books and finishing homework.
Learners plant, water, weed and harvest, and keep simple records of growth. It links Agriculture, Science and Maths.
Learners observe, test and make simple things — plants, water, the body, simple tools. At home: watch which wet cloth dries fastest — in the sun, shade or wind.
If worried, visit a clinic, paediatrician or a county assessment centre. Early help makes a big difference.
Senior school covers three years for learners about 16–18, per the 2019 framework.
Three years where learners follow a pathway that matches their interests. KICD's framework gives the age as about 16–18.
Communication and Collaboration; Self-efficacy; Critical Thinking and Problem Solving; Creativity and Imagination; Citizenship; Digital Literacy; Learning to Le
The framework names seven, including communication and collaboration, critical thinking and problem solving, and creativity and imagination.
Tracks: Languages and Literature, and Humanities & Business Studies. Suits learners who enjoy reading, writing, people and society.
How the body moves, trains and stays healthy, plus playing and organising sport. Subjects: Sports and Recreation, Physical Education.
Ask: What do you enjoy doing even when nobody tells you to? Fixing a radio, reading novels, drawing, playing football?
CBC was launched in 2017 and phased in grade by grade. You may also hear it called CBE (Competency Based Education).
The 2019 curriculum framework says children enter Grade 1 at about six years old. Check your school's admission rules.
Attend meetings, read notes and ask questions early when something is not clear.
Tracks: Pure Sciences, Applied Sciences and Technical Studies. Suits learners who enjoy maths, science, building and technology.
Doctors, nurses, engineers, computer experts, farmers and agronomists, builders, electricians, mechanics, pilots and media technicians.
Taking turns, sharing toys, and telling others what they need in words.
Hands-on skills for building, fixing and making things. Subjects: Aviation, Building Construction, Electricity, Metal Work, Power Mechanics, Woodwork, Media Tec
Cover the notes and try to recall, or use flashcards. This shows what you really know.
KICD lists CRE, IRE and HRE for Grades 1–3.
KICD's course book lists show three pathways: STEM, Social Sciences, and Arts and Sports Science.
The three pathways are STEM, Social Sciences, and Arts and Sports Science.
KICD's course book lists show three pathways: STEM, Social Sciences, and Arts and Sports Science.
The Teachers Service Commission registers and employs teachers for public schools, and posts, promotes and disciplines them.
Technical and vocational colleges teach practical trades and diplomas, such as electrical work, plumbing, catering or ICT.
The course book lists show both Core Mathematics and Essential Mathematics. Ask your school which one fits your child's track.
Pre-primary has two years. PP1 comes first, then PP2, then the child moves to Grade 1.
The 2019 curriculum framework places senior school learners at about 16 to 18 years old. Some learners will be younger or older.
Values in the CBC include respect, responsibility, care and compassion, and honesty. Small children learn them by copying adults and by gentle praise.
Taking turns, caring for books, and greeting others politely.
The framework names values including responsibility, respect, excellence, care and compassion, understanding and tolerance, honesty and trustworthiness, trust,
Teachers notice what a child can do: hold a pencil, count to ten, join in a song. This is the main way young children are assessed.
Instead of separate biology, chemistry and physics, the ideas are taught together. Separate science subjects appear later, in the senior school STEM pathway.
Eight years of primary, four of secondary and four of university, introduced in 1985.
Lower primary (Grade 1–3) adds learning areas such as English, Kiswahili and Mathematics. See the Lower primary map.
Learners use their knowledge and skills on a real community need, planned with community partners, then reflect on it in class.
Learners use what they know to meet a real need in the community, working with community partners, then think back on what they learned.
The course book lists do not say which senior school subjects every learner must take. Check with your school.
